data.narrative:
Cellcolabs is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Mattias Bernow that has raised $37M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 peers in Biotech & Health (3 public, 8 private), including notable private names such as Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals, alongside public anchors RXRX, TEM, and ONT.L.

Stage-progression methodology is the sole applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier for progression from Series A to subsequent stages yields an implied valuation of $74M. The peer-median method could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Biotech & Health subset (zero narrow-filtered peers met the minimum threshold of three datapoints). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples—the three public peers trade at a 7.4x median multiple—cannot be executed without the target's disclosed revenue, which remains unavailable for private-stage companies.

The quantitative analysis supports a valuation range of $63M to $85M, with a central estimate of $74M. This range reflects typical variance around stage-progression assumptions rather than cross-method triangulation. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable transaction multiples at identical stage/sector intersection and lack of revenue visibility, both of which constrain precision. The valuation remains highly contingent on progress metrics and capital deployment efficiency post-Series A.
